subject: Unexpected usage surge and invoice variance — next steps & timeline
messages:
From: Aaron Zhao <aaron@loglab.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: finance@loglab.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:47 -0700
Subject: Spike on 5/20 invoice — requesting clarification

Hi Stephanie,

We noticed a sharp spike on our May 20th usage line item — roughly 6x our expected token count for peak hours. That produced an unexpected ~$4.8k charge on the provisional invoice. Can you help confirm whether this was legitimate usage from our integration or whether there was a duplication/counting issue on your side?

I attached a small slice of our internal telemetry (see attached CSV) that maps session IDs to timestamps; happy to share more. Our finance lead needs an initial read by EOD Monday — can you confirm receipt and an ETA for an investigation?

Thanks,
Aaron
Finance Manager
Logistics Labs

Attachment: usage-sample-20.csv (CSV 14KB)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Zhao <aaron@loglab.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:04:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike on 5/20 invoice — requesting clarification

Aaron — thanks for flagging and for the sample. I received the CSV.

Quick note on process: we'll triage this with infra and metering immediately and aim to provide a preliminary root-cause note by Monday morning PST. If we identify an internal counting error, we'll produce a corrective credit and a short postmortem with mitigations.

I looped in Dev (metering/runtime) and Marissa from Billing so they can pull traces and the provisional invoice.

Next steps from our side:
- Dev will run a matching job against your session IDs and our request logs.
- Marissa will flag the provisional invoice in our billing pipeline to prevent auto-finalization until we've reconciled.

I'll keep you posted with timestamped updates.

—Stephanie
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Aaron Zhao <aaron@loglab.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:17:03 -07:00
Subject: RE: Spike on 5/20 invoice — matching logs and initial findings

Aaron / Stephanie — preliminary results below after matching the session IDs Aaron sent against our request stream for 2027-05-20 (range 00:00–23:59 UTC):

Summary:
- We observed two anomalous conditions that together explain the elevated token count for several sessions: a transient retry loop in a customer-side worker around 14:12–14:19 UTC that replayed identical 1xx requests, and a short-lived inflight-kv duplication bug in our batching layer between 14:12:30–14:14:20 UTC that resulted in duplicate token accounting for ~8% of the replayed requests.
- Total estimated overcount attributable to the duplication bug: ~11,600 tokens (approx $720 at your current plan).
- The majority of the observed surge is attributable to the customer-side retries (which produced genuine additional requests) — our accounting matches those extra requests.

Actions taken:
- We've flagged the affected metering window and paused invoice finalization for LogLab's May cycle.
- I attached a CSV extract (redwood-usage-sample-20270520.csv) showing request_id, timestamp, model, token_count, and a dup_flag column where we detected the duplication.
- We have a short internal incident note attached (prelim-incident-notes-20270522.pdf).

Follow-ups planned:
1) Postmortem: engineering will publish a short postmortem by 2027-05-27 with root cause and mitigations for the batching-layer duplication.
2) Credits: billing will propose a corrective credit for the counted-dup tokens once the postmortem is finalized.
3) Customer guidance: we'll provide recommendation to suppress automatic worker-retries for idempotent inference requests (or add deterministic client-side de-dup keying).

Aaron — do you have a list of session IDs that you consider business-critical for May 20 reconciliation? If so, we can prioritize exact-match reconciliation for those.

—Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-usage-sample-20270520.csv (CSV 42KB)
Attachment: prelim-incident-notes-20270522.pdf (PDF 28KB)
From: Aaron Zhao <aaron@loglab.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:33:11 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike on 5/20 invoice — matching logs and initial findings

Thanks for the quick look, Dev — that explanation makes sense. The retry loop came from a worker we pushed on 5/20 for a short A/B run; we missed rate-limiting behavior in that release.

We'd like Redwood to handle the duplication-only charge (the 11,600 tokens you flagged) as a credit; we accept responsibility for the genuine retries but not the internal duplication bug. For reconciliation purposes, I'll send a small list of 14 session IDs (business critical) this afternoon; please prioritize those.

Also: our procurement team asked for an ETA on the official postmortem and a written credit timeline so they can close the invoice on their side. They need the credit posted within this billing cycle if possible.

Aaron

On Tue, May 25, 2027 at 10:40 AM, marissa_cole@redwood.ai wrote:
> Hi Aaron — thanks for confirming. We'll provisionally prepare a credit line once engineering finalizes the duplication accounting.
>
> Marissa Cole
> Billing Operations
> Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Zhao <aaron@loglab.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike on 5/20 invoice — next steps & timeline

Aaron — quick update and committed timeline:

1) Engineering postmortem (final): scheduled for 2027-05-27 11:59 PT. It will include the root cause, duplicate-token accounting, and a proposed software mitigation. We'll share the Drive link as soon as it's ready: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3CcIncidentAudit

2) Credit timeline: Marissa will issue a billing credit covering the duplication-only amount (~11,600 tokens / ~$720) within 3 business days after the postmortem is published. We'll mark the credit in your provisional invoice so your procurement can close the payment cycle.

3) Reconciliation priority: please send the 14 session IDs you mentioned; Dev will prioritize exact-match reconciliation for those by EOD Wednesday.

4) Preventive guidance: we'll supply a short checklist to reduce retry-induced surges (idempotency keys, tighter client-side backoff, and a recommended server-side rate-limiter config) as part of the postmortem.

If this plan works, I'll follow up with the credit memo and the postmortem link. Apologies for the friction — we want to make this right and ensure it doesn't recur.

Best,
—Stephanie
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
